To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the “up-promoter”, zwfL1 mutation of the constitutive glucose 6-phospate dehydrogenase gene (zwf), is located in the 3′-noncoding region and increases the rate of transcription by 18-fold.
the zwf promoter is located in the 5' untranslated region of the gene and mutations that increase expression of this promoter can be isolated.

(1) a mutation in the promoter region of the zwf gene of E. coli results in the production of a constitutively active enzyme; (2) this constitutively active promoter is a high-level mutation, which is the highest-level mutation known in E. coli; (3) the mutation is in the region of the promoter that is involved in the binding of the cAMP-CAP complex; (4) the mutation increases the affinity of the cAMP complex for the promoter
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the regulation of the expression of the structural gene for glucose-6-phosphate dehydogenase in Eschericha coli.
the genetic control of the biosynthesis of enzymes in microorganisms.
the study of the molecular mechanisms of gene regulation and expression in bacteria.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a mutation of a promoter of a gene for an enzyme of the pentose phosphate cycle in E. coli increases the level of expression of this enzyme 18-fold.
the up-promoter mutations of the zwf locus are located at the 5′ end of the zwf mRNA, that is, at the promoter end of the structural gene.

the zwfL1 mutation is a “up-promoter mutation” of the zwf gene, that it is not a “constitutive” mutation, that it does not alter the specificity of the enzyme, and that the level of expression of the zwfL2 mutation is 18-fold higher than that of the wild-type.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have found that the promoter of zwf is unusually strong, and that the “up-promoter mutation” is not a simple increase in the strength of the promoter, but a more complex alteration of its structure.
the “up-promoter”, zwfL2 mutant has an altered DNA sequence in the 5′-untranslated region of the gene, which is located about 200 nucleotides upstream of the start codon.
mutations in the zwf promoter region can increase its expression by up to 200-fold.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in addition to mutations affecting the promoter itself, mutations can occur in the structural gene which affect the efficiency of the promoter.
, in the wild-type, zwf is expressed at a level which is not limiting for the biosynthetic pathways in which it participates.
it is possible to make a bacterial gene 18 times more highly expressed than its normal level.
